llm.summary: The skill is a coherent P2P messaging and file-transfer portal, but it requests broad authority and contains serious access-control, credential-handling, installer, and remote-message safety flaws.

dimensions.detail: The requested API keys, OpenClaw hooks token, SSH key, public HTTPS/WSS Portal, and file-transfer authority are substantial but purpose-related; concern comes from disabled TLS verification, missing URL validation, unauthenticated public endpoints, and raw shared secrets sent to portals.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installers perform SSH deployment, sudo package installs, Nginx and systemd setup, dependency installation, remote git clone of the current repository head, and destructive replacement of /opt/agent-p2p; several command strings interpolate user-controlled values through shell=True.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions ask the agent to manage VPS infrastructure and recommend full exec permissions with confirmation disabled; ENV.md also normalizes checking and printing local files that contain API keys, hook tokens, and the admin password.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is expected for an always-on bridge and Portal, but the package enables user and system systemd services, rewrites OpenClaw configuration, stores secrets in plaintext files, and one deployment path runs the Portal as root.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: P2P messaging, file transfer, a VPS Portal, and an OpenClaw bridge are consistent with the stated purpose, but the implementation exposes high-impact capabilities including Portal administration, owner chat, shared keys, file upload/download, and OpenClaw wake-hook access with weak separation between roles.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a test environment unless you are prepared to audit and fix it first. Before production use, require authentication and role separation on all Portal APIs, remove the hardcoded/default passwords, stop printing or storing plaintext secrets, validate contact portal URLs, restore TLS verification, sanitize downloaded filenames and UI rendering, add file-size and storage limits, avoid shell=True, pin deployed code and dependencies, and keep OpenClaw wake-hook processing isolated from remote message instructions.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: the artifacts document secret locations and include commands to print gateway.env, openclaw.json tokens, and the saved admin password; configuration lookup is expected, but routine plaintext disclosure is not.
[TT5] unexpected: Accepted: auto_install.py places the interactive replacement admin password into an SSH command executed with shell=True, creating a real command-injection risk during a privileged deployment workflow.
[TT3] expected: Partly downgraded but still concerning: sending API keys and content to configured portals is core functionality, but the artifacts do not validate portal destinations and directly send shared keys and file chunks to contact-provided URLs.
[TM1] unexpected: Accepted: installer helpers and SSH/curl/nslookup invocations use shell=True with domain, host, path, URL, token, or password values, which is not necessary for the stated purpose.
[PE3] expected: Mostly expected: SSH-key references are part of VPS deployment guidance and CONFIG.md recommends a dedicated key, but this still contributes to the need for careful review.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted: vps/main.py has unauthenticated key creation and several unauthenticated sensitive endpoints, and get_token accepts ap2p_ keys for endpoints that return or modify high-value Portal data.
[T01] unexpected: Accepted: local/bridge.py forwards remote guest and contact message content into the OpenClaw wake-hook text field without treating it as untrusted data, while the skill asks for broad execution permissions.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: artifact evidence shows a hardcoded default admin password in vps/main.py, disabled TLS verification in clients, stored XSS in admin contact rendering, local file overwrite on download filenames, unbounded file storage, and unsafe shell construction.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as a supporting concern: dependencies are not pinned and VPS deployment pulls the latest GitHub branch rather than the reviewed artifact or a fixed signed commit.
